narr: Two rounds of storms moved across southeast Minnesota on July 23rd. The first occurred in the afternoon and produced two tornadoes, wind damage and large hail. A brief EF0 tornado occurred south of Fremont (Winona County) that produced mainly tree damage. Another EF0 tornado touched down just north of Houston (Houston County) and damaged a barn and trees along its path. The storms also produced high winds that damaged structures in Claremont (Dodge County), blew down trees in numerous locations, and produced 66 mph gusts in downtown Rochester (Olmsted County) and near Brownsdale (Mower County) and Sheldon (Houston County). The largest reported hail was quarter sized near Oronoco (Olmsted County). The second round of storms occurred in the late evening, producing dime sized hail near Spring Valley (Fillmore County) before moving into northeast Iowa. Houston County declared a state of emergency following the storms.
ev: Radar estimates indicated 2 to 3 inches of rain fell across the eastern sections of Mower County. This resulted in some flash flooding that sent water over a road east of Grand Meadow.
